question: Can Simon oversee the company without operating it — one queue of what is waiting for him, a pause that stops everything outward at once, a denial that sticks and teaches, a steer on which offer to lead with — and a dashboard whose every number is the journal's, not a summary someone typed?
why: Simon's AI-first company spec (2026-10-28), build step 6: 'the oversight layer (flags, dashboard, steering)': approval gates on money, deals, big or novel public claims, high-stakes replies, risky or precedent-setting actions and the ledger switch; a dashboard of leads, conversions, content, signals, deliveries and library growth; direction and course-correction.

design.queue: src/oversight.mjs queue(journal): one item per 'asked' event — what it is, the hash of its exact text, its flags, and its state: waiting, approved, denied or withdrawn (from later approved / steer-deny / steer-withdraw entries for the same hash).
design.steer: Simon's steering is journal entries of kind 'steer' (by simon, or rehearsal in a rehearsal): { pause: true | false }, { deny: <text hash>, note }, { withdraw: <text hash> }, { focus: <offer id> }.
design.mayGo: mayGo(journal, hash): approved, not denied, not withdrawn, and not paused at that moment. Outward steps ask mayGo before they go.
design.focus: pickWithFocus(text, focus): the offer the person's own words call for; only when their words tie between offers does Simon's focus decide, and only if it is one of the tied offers.
design.dashboard: dashboard(journal): signals (all, eligible, market), leads (qualified, converted), content (drafted, asked, approved, sent), deliveries (handed, recorded), library size, queue (waiting, approved, denied), steering entries — each a count of the journal's own entries.

claims.claim: Every dashboard number equals an independent plain count of the journal's entries, on the step 4 and step 5 journals together, and the combined journal verifies.
The pause: on a journal where an item is approved, mayGo is true; after a pause entry it is false for that item and every other approved item; after an unpause it is true again.
claims.pass: true, all false while paused, true

claims.claim: A denial sticks and teaches: a denied item's mayGo is false even if it is approved afterwards, its queue state is denied, and its note is returned by notesFor for the next draft.

Focus steers only ties: with focus digi, the tied lead (L6, 'could my own model collect cards?') gets digi; the explicit leads L1, L2 and L3 keep their own offers; a focus that is not one of the tied offers changes nothing.

scope: The dashboard is computed from the rehearsal journals of steps 4 and 5 (fixture leads, rehearsal approvals). Simon's real steering arrives as journal entries Kar writes on his word in chat, quoted.
